prompt: A clean, straight-on printed label sheet titled 'PARCEL DISPATCH QR SHEET'. Subtitle 'Depot dispatch codes -- one scannable QR per parcel ID'. The sheet shows SIX separate QR codes arranged in a 2-columns by 3-rows grid. Beside each QR code, print the label 'ASSET TAG:' and then the exact tag string that this QR code must encode. The six tag strings, in reading order (left-to-right, then top-to-bottom), are: PKG-7741-X, PKG-3092-Q, PKG-5518-M, PKG-8267-R, PKG-1934-T, PKG-6405-K. CRITICAL: each QR code must be a REAL, SCANNABLE QR code that actually decodes to EXACTLY the tag string printed beside it (standard black-and-white QR modules with the three square finder patterns in the corners and a quiet white border). Do not draw a decorative QR-like texture -- the codes must scan. Print exactly six QR codes and their six captions, nothing else.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict a printed warehouse/dispatch label sheet showing an array of QR codes each captioned with an asset/parcel tag. Ignoring artistic quality, does the image actually DEPICT that requested subject -- a sheet of QR-code tiles with captions? A photo, scan or clean diagram all count as yes. Answer NO only if it shows a blank card, plain panel, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_ntiles: How many separate QR-code tiles (square black-and-white 2D codes) are printed on this sheet? Give a whole number only.

steps.target: one printed QR code tile -- one square block of black and white modules on the label sheet

steps.read_crop: Does this cut-out show ONE whole square QR code, its complete black-and-white pattern with the dark square markers at its corners, rather than part of a code, two codes together, or a line of printed text? Answer yes or no only.
